proposed_survivor_patch.title: Ivanka Trump’s Company Receives Three Provisional Chinese Trademark Approvals
proposed_survivor_patch.description_short: China provisionally approved three trademarks for Ivanka Trump’s company on April 6, 2017, the day she dined with Xi Jinping.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_medium: China provisionally approved three trademarks for Ivanka Trump’s company on April 6, 2017, the day Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner dined with Xi Jinping at Mar-a-Lago. CNN identified the marks as covering jewelry, spa services and bags. The same report said 16 marks were already fully registered. Timing does not establish intervention, causation or improper treatment.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_long: On April 6, 2017, Chinese authorities granted preliminary approval to three trademark applications from Ivanka Trump’s company, according to CNN and Associated Press excerpts supplied in the source-worker packet. AP reported that the approvals coincided with Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner dining with Xi Jinping and his wife at Mar-a-Lago. CNN identified the marks as covering jewelry, spa services and bags, based on Chinese trademark documents it reviewed. The 16 mentioned in the earlier account referred to marks the company already held as fully registered; it was not the number newly approved that day. CNN’s report was published April 18, while AP’s follow-up appeared April 19, so those dates describe reporting rather than the approval event. The timing raised an ethics question because Ivanka Trump held a White House advisory role while her company received foreign trademark approvals. The supplied excerpts do not show that Donald or Ivanka Trump intervened in the process, that the dinner caused the approvals, that officials treated the applications improperly, or that the approvals produced a particular commercial return. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said trademark applications were handled according to law and equal-protection principles. This account records the approvals and their timing while leaving any allegation of favoritism unproven.

terminal_record.title: NPR Reported DOGE Staff Had Nuclear Network Accounts; DOE Said They Were Never Used
terminal_record.description_short: NPR reported two DOGE employees had accounts on classified nuclear networks; DOE said the accounts were never activated or accessed.
terminal_record.description_medium: An NPR report published April 28, 2025 said two DOGE employees had accounts on classified networks used for nuclear information. The Department of Energy said the accounts had never been activated or accessed. NPR also explained that an account’s presence on a network did not by itself grant access to classified data. The reporting documents an account-creation and oversight concern, not confirmed viewing or extraction of nuclear files.
terminal_record.description_long: On April 28, 2025, NPR reported that two Department of Government Efficiency employees had accounts on classified networks used by the National Nuclear Security Administration and the Defense Department. NPR cited two sources who said the accounts had been present for at least two weeks. The Department of Energy first denied that the employees had accessed the networks, then said the accounts had been created but never activated or accessed. NPR also reported that merely appearing on a network directory would not by itself give an employee access to classified data stored there. The supported event is the creation and listing of the accounts, followed by reporting about them and the department’s explanation. The reporting does not establish that either employee viewed, copied, or otherwise accessed nuclear weapons information. It also does not establish the frozen entry’s claims of an unauthorized file breach, foreign business conflicts, or an immediate federal investigation. This repair narrows the entry to the documented access-control concern and preserves the agency’s response.
terminal_record.date_basis: Date of the NPR report documenting the accounts and DOE response; the accounts were reportedly present earlier.

terminal_record.title: Rubio Reports More Than 300 Visa Revocations, Confirms Ozturk Visa Action
terminal_record.description_short: Rubio said the State Department may have revoked over 300 visas and confirmed Tufts student Rumeysa Ozturk's visa revocation; he gave no case-specific reason.
terminal_record.description_medium: At a March 27, 2025, press event in Guyana, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the State Department may have revoked more than 300 visas, including student and visitor visas, and said he signed each action. He confirmed Tufts doctoral student Rumeysa Ozturk's visa was revoked but did not explain her specific conduct. Independent reporting describes her arrest and prior campus opinion writing, not a general Israel-criticism trigger.
terminal_record.description_long: On March 27, 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the State Department may have revoked more than 300 visas. He described the total as including student and visitor visas and said he had signed each action. He made the remarks in Guyana after federal agents detained Tufts University doctoral student Rumeysa Ozturk and the State Department revoked her visa. The Associated Press reported that Ozturk's lawyer said no charges had been filed. AP also reported that she was one of four students who wrote a Tufts Daily opinion piece criticizing the university's response to demands for divestment from companies tied to Israel. Reuters reported Rubio did not explain what specific conduct by Ozturk justified revoking her visa. He listed vandalism, harassment, building takeovers and other disruptive conduct as grounds for taking away student visas, but did not say Ozturk had done those things. He said the standard in her case involved support for movements contrary to U.S. foreign policy. The reporting does not show that every visa in the reported total was revoked for criticism of Israel, for a social media post, or for one common reason; it leaves individual grounds unresolved.
